Chapter 11: Facing Resistance and Navigating Change
You know, change almost never comes easy—especially when it means letting go of the things we’ve always relied on.
For teachers, parents, or managers, just the thought of moving beyond rewards and punishments can feel pretty unsettling.
There’s this fear, right? That if we stop using those levers, nothing will get done.
Old habits die hard, and let’s be honest—the pressure to get results is always there.
Picture this: in one school, a teacher decided to stop using stickers and grades as motivators.
At first, the students were totally confused—some even came up and asked for their rewards back.
The teacher felt that urge to just go back to the old way, but she stuck with it, focusing on building real relationships and supporting her students’ independence.
And over time, guess what happened? The students actually started to adjust.
They began taking more responsibility, and the classroom slowly transformed into a place where everyone was truly engaged.
At home, it’s often the same story. One parent chose to stop using screen time as a bargaining chip.
Those first few days? They were rough—filled with arguments and pushback.
But the parent kept focusing on real conversations and problem-solving.
And little by little, the child began to cooperate—not for a prize, but because it mattered to the family.
In the workplace, a manager ran into skepticism when she suggested ending the bonus system.
Some employees worried their motivation would disappear.
But instead of pushing through, the manager brought everyone into the conversation, inviting their ideas and listening to their concerns.
Together, they built a new system—one based on trust and shared goals.
Sure, the transition wasn’t perfect. But in the end, the team came out stronger than before.
One thing becomes clear: resistance is just part of the process.
People need time to adjust—to trust that this new direction will actually work.
The real key? Staying patient, listening, and keeping the focus on relationships and growth.
Most of us don’t realize just how deeply those old systems are woven into our routines.
It honestly takes a lot of courage to try something different, and even more persistence to see it through.
But here’s the thing—the rewards are worth it.
Real engagement, deeper connections, and motivation that actually lasts.
The path forward isn’t always simple, but it is possible.
With patience, support, and a willingness to keep learning, anyone can move beyond rewards and punishments, and create spaces where people really thrive.
